title: I-30 photos Dallas

pageHeader.title: Roadside Views between Rockwall and East Dallas

text:
The LBJ East project began in 2021, and in 2022 the original interchange at I-635 LBJ Freeway was demolished. The original interchange opened in 1970 was the first modern-design four-level interchange in North Texas, and was the first of six interchanges which used the distinctive "double T" central pylon. The I-30 archive photos include a view of the original interchange.

Projects to widen the freeway and add frontage roads on new bridges at the Lake Ray Hubbard crossing started in July 2021 (Bass Pro Dr. to Dalrock Rd.) and March 2023 (Dalrock Rd. to SH 205). The section from Dalrock to SH 205 is scheduled for completion in January 2027.

TxDOT has long-term plans to rebuild and expand the freeway from I-635 to I-45. This work will occur in the 2030s or 2040s.

As of June 2025 these photos remain accurate except as noted.

images.caption: Looking west from Horizon Street, with lake Ray Hubbard ahead

imageStatus.note: Main lanes were widened to 4 in each direction and frontage roads on new bridges were added. Work on this section began in March 2023 with completion scheduled for January 2027.

images.caption: Looking west from the DalRock road overpass, which is on a peninsula in Lake Ray Hubbard.

imageStatus.note: Main lanes were widened to 4 in each direction and frontage roads on new bridges were added. A new direct connection ramp from eastbound I-30 to northbound Dalrock was built. Work on this section began in July 2021 with completion in 2025.

images.caption: At Bass Pro Road, looking west.

imageStatus.note: The interchange for the Bush Turnpike was built in the area ahead, opening in 2011. The I-30 main lanes remain about the same.
